title: Microsoft Purview DLP: count of labelled attachments condition for Exchange Online
summary: The briefing is supported by the roadmap, the supplied Microsoft notice and Microsoft Learn. Minor corrections should add the omitted wizard heading to both portal paths and remove checklist checks for label publication and administrator membership that have no corresponding control row.

claims.claim: Microsoft Purview DLP is adding the condition named Count of labeled documents is greater than.
claims.quote: This release introduces a new condition for Exchange Online policies: “Count of labeled documents is greater than.”

claims.claim: The condition is available for Exchange Online DLP policies.
claims.quote: The condition is available for Exchange Online DLP policies

claims.claim: The condition does not apply to SharePoint, OneDrive, Teams or Endpoint DLP.
claims.quote: does not apply to SharePoint, OneDrive, Teams, or Endpoint DLP workloads.

claims.where: summary; What's changing; Risk assessment: Data exposure
claims.claim: It counts attachments carrying a matching sensitivity label in a single email message, rather than unlabelled attachments.
claims.quote: This condition evaluates the number of attachments in an email message that carry a matching sensitivity label.

claims.where: summary; What's changing; Risk assessment: Data exposure
claims.claim: The configured threshold is strict greater-than, so a count equal to the threshold does not trigger the condition.
claims.quote: The condition uses a strict greater-than threshold.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions
claims.claim: When the threshold is exceeded, the DLP rule triggers and applies its configured actions.
claims.quote: When the count exceeds a defined threshold, the DLP rule is triggered, and configured actions are applied.

claims.claim: The roadmap describes detection of high-volume exfiltration in which individually low-risk files collectively represent significant risk.
claims.quote: This capability enables detection of high-volume data exfiltration scenarios, where multiple sensitive files—individually low-risk—collectively represent a significant compliance or security risk.

claims.claim: The roadmap says existing conditions evaluate content but provide no controls based on labelled-attachment volume.
claims.quote: Existing conditions evaluate file content, but do not provide controls based on the volume of labeled attachments.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Data exposure
claims.claim: Each matching attachment is counted individually, including duplicate copies of a file.
claims.quote: Each attachment with a matching sensitivity label will be counted individually, including duplicate copies of the same file.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Data exposure
claims.claim: Selecting several labels evaluates the combined count of all matching attachments.
claims.quote: When multiple sensitivity labels are selected in a rule, the condition evaluates the combined count of all matching attachments.

claims.where: What's changing; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: A threshold of 3 triggers at 4 or more matching attachments.
claims.quote: For example, a threshold of 3 is triggered when 4 or more matching attachments are detected.

claims.claim: The protection wrapper of encrypted, rights-protected attachments is excluded to avoid double-counting.
claims.quote: Encrypted (rights-protected) attachments: protection wrapper is excluded to prevent double-counting.

claims.where: What's changing; Why it matters; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: Administrators can combine this condition with existing content-based DLP conditions and actions.
claims.quote: The feature provides an additional volume-based signal that can be combined with existing content-based DLP conditions for layered protection.

claims.where: front matter: defaultState; summary; Why it matters; Governance controls; rationale: risk
claims.claim: The condition is admin-opt-in and is not automatically enabled through existing policies, so leaving it unconfigured changes nothing.
claims.quote: The feature is administrator configured and is not enabled automatically through existing policies.

claims.claim: No action is required before rollout.
claims.quote: No action is required before rollout.

claims.where: What's changing; controls[0].note; Governance controls; Open questions
claims.claim: The Learn Exchange conditions reference and cited policy-creation article do not yet list the new condition or its specific admin path.
claims.quote: Searched: Purview DLP "Count of labeled documents is greater than" admin condition reference. Opened dlp-policy-reference, dlp-exchange-conditions-and-actions and dlp-create-policy-cc-email; searched count, label and threshold; no entry for the new condition.

claims.claim: The supplied notice describes no identity or authentication change.
claims.quote: Searched: read the full supplied MC1508235, including What will happen and Compliance considerations, for identity and authentication changes; none is described.

claims.claim: The notice says available information does not indicate that Entra ID group membership can control the condition itself.
claims.quote: The available information does not indicate that the condition itself can be controlled through Entra ID group membership.

claims.where: Scope; Risk assessment: Security & identity; controls[0].note
claims.claim: The deployment article requires membership in Compliance administrator, Compliance data administrator, Information Protection, Information Protection Admin or Security administrator to create and deploy DLP policies.
claims.quote:
The account you use to create and deploy policies must be a member of one of these role groups:
- Compliance administrator
- Compliance data administrator
- Information Protection
- Information Protection Admin
- Security administrator

claims.claim: A blocking action can stop messages matched by the rule.
claims.quote: Block: The user activity is blocked no matter what. You can audit the event, raise alerts and notifications.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: No policy actions are enforced in Run the policy in simulation mode.
claims.quote: Run the policy in simulation mode: No policy actions are enforced, events are audited.

claims.claim: Events are audited in simulation mode.
claims.quote: Run the policy in simulation mode: No policy actions are enforced, events are audited.

claims.claim: Microsoft recommends testing policies in simulation or audit mode before enforcing actions.
claims.quote: Test policies in simulation or audit mode before enabling enforcement actions.

claims.claim: Microsoft recommends reviewing existing Exchange Online DLP policies for possible attachment-count thresholds.

claims.where: Governance guidance: Before rollout; Cost and licensing

claims.claim: Microsoft recommends updating internal documentation where supported Exchange Online conditions are documented.
claims.quote: Update internal DLP administration documentation if supported Exchange Online conditions are documented within your organization.

claims.claim: The printed Microsoft Purview portal path reaches Conditions > Add condition in the Exchange policy wizard.
claims.quote: On the Define policy settings page, the Create or customize advanced DLP rules option should already be selected.
claims.fix: In controls[0].ui.path and the rendered table, use 'Data loss prevention > Policies > + Create policy > Enterprise applications & devices > Custom > Custom > Exchange email > Define policy settings > Create or customize advanced DLP rules > Create rule > Conditions > Add condition'. Retain the note that this page does not document the new condition.

claims.claim: No documented PowerShell parameter sets this specific labelled-attachment count condition in New-DlpComplianceRule or Set-DlpComplianceRule.
claims.quote: Searched: "Count of labeled documents" New-DlpComplianceRule and Set-DlpComplianceRule threshold. Opened both cmdlet references and dlp-exchange-conditions-and-actions; searched count/label/attachment parameter names and descriptions; no matching setting documented.

claims.claim: The printed Microsoft Purview portal path reaches Run the policy in simulation mode after the rule is saved.
claims.quote: On the Define policy settings page, the Create or customize advanced DLP rules option should already be selected.
claims.fix: In controls[1].ui.path and the rendered table, use 'Data loss prevention > Policies > + Create policy > Enterprise applications & devices > Custom > Custom > Exchange email > Define policy settings > Create or customize advanced DLP rules > Create rule > Run the policy in simulation mode'. Retain the note that the rule is saved before choosing simulation mode.

claims.claim: Set-DlpCompliancePolicy -Identity <policy name> -Mode TestWithoutNotifications sets the named policy to simulation without notifications.
claims.quote:
The Mode parameter specifies the action and notification level of the DLP policy. Valid values are:
TestWithoutNotifications: Simulation mode where no actions are taken, and no notifications are sent.

claims.claim: Mode also accepts Enable, Disable and TestWithNotifications.
claims.quote:
Enable: The policy is enabled for actions and notifications. This value is the default.
Disable: The policy is disabled.
TestWithNotifications: Simulation mode where no actions are taken, but notifications are sent.

claims.claim: The wizard offers simulation mode on the page after the rule is saved.
claims.quote:
39. Select Save.
40. Select Next, then select Run the policy in simulation mode.

claims.claim: Policy impact in simulation mode can be monitored in the DLP simulation mode overview and DLP Activity explorer.
claims.quote: While in this state, you can monitor the impact of the policy in the DLP simulation mode overview and the DLP Activity explorer console.

claims.claim: Simulation and enforcement state control the whole DLP policy, rather than this condition alone.
claims.quote: Turn it on | All targeted location instances | - All configured actions are enforced on user activities

claims.claim: The notice states strict greater-than semantics but supplies no minimum or maximum threshold value.
claims.quote: Searched: read supplied MC1508235 for threshold minimum, maximum and range; only strict greater-than and the example of 3 are given. Learn search for "Count of labeled documents" threshold minimum maximum and the opened DLP reference give no range.

claims.claim: The checklist asks readers to check label publication and administrator role-group membership, but neither control has a table row.
claims.quote: Check which sensitivity labels are published and in use; Confirm which of the role groups listed under Scope your DLP administrators belong to. The controls table covers only the attachment-count condition and policy state.
claims.fix: Remove the Before rollout bullets beginning 'Check which sensitivity labels are published and in use' and 'Confirm which of the role groups listed under Scope'. Retain the factual labelling and permissions discussion elsewhere; do not add control rows.
